thread:
zoe: Quick sync — Sales asked for a clear "escape path" for customers who overcommit. Want a playbook we can point to during negotiations. Can we agree on deterministic options?
jordan: Finance: need 3 canonical options: (1) Soft-commit (credits rollover), (2) Tranche-commit (step-down schedule), (3) Hard-commit (ETF on shortfall). Each has different P&L shapes.
mira: Legal: prefer explicit formulas + examples. Also need notice windows and a maximum frequency (e.g., 2 adjustments/year). Avoid fuzzy language.
kai: Ops: enforcement must be automatic. If Soft-commit, ledger needs rollover buckets. Tranche-commit needs scheduled scale-down windows to free capacity. Hard-commit is easiest technically.
rachel: Sales: customers want flexibility, but also simple pricing at close. Recommend default to Tranche-commit for enterprise and Soft-commit as a pilot incentive.
li: UX: customers will misread credits. We should show a clear sim before they accept any change: current_commit, new_commit, estimated_fee_or_credit, next_eligible_change_date.
billing-bot: Note: current billing schema supports `unused_credits` but not expiration. We'll need `credit_expiry_ts` and `commit_tranche_schedule`.
zoe: Proposal to align: Default product offering = Tranche-commit (quarterly step-down up to 30% per quarter), Pilot offering = Soft-commit (single 60d rollover at 80% value), and Special cases = Hard-commit negotiated with ETF.
jordan: Add sample math for the docs: 
`shortfall_units = max(0, committed - actual_30d)`
`ETF = shortfall_units * unit_price * haircut`
example: committed=1,000,000 tokens/month, actual=600,000 -> shortfall=400,000; unit=$0.00025; haircut=0.25 -> ETF=$25.
mira: I'll draft three contract clause templates mapping to each option and include the math + example tables. Also add breach and outage carveouts.
kai: Implementation checklist: ledger fields (`credit_balance`,`credit_expiry_ts`,`commit_tranche_schedule`), API validation for `PATCH /subscription` to block illegal shrinkage, and routing flags to drain reserved pools during tranche windows.
li: UX checklist: downgrade modal + estimator, billing page tile for credits with expiry timeline, email workflow for notifications. I'll mock the UI flows and copy.
rachel: Sales ops: need templated SOW language for pilots and a script for negotiation (what we can promise vs not). Also need a one-pager we can give legal-signed customers.
jordan: Finance will run 5 sensitivity sims (rollover @70/80/90%, tranche agresstion rates, ETF at 10/25/50%) and publish a recommended default.
zoe: OK action items: Mira draft clauses by Tue, Jordan run sims by Wed, Kai estimate implementation effort + risk by Thu, Li ship UX mocks by Thu, Rachel draft sales one-pager by Fri. Block tier changes until legal signoff on default.
mira: One more ask: include a sample dispute flow (how customers raise a measurement dispute). We should log `usage_provenance` for auditability.
kai: Good call. We'll add `usage_provenance` to export logs and attach hashes for tamper evidence.
zoe: Thanks all. I'll add this to the roadmap as "Commit Flexibility Playbook" and schedule an approval review next week. Ping me if you want to test edge-cases. :white_check_mark:
